# 0.2.0 Stereo VRS

User-approved direction: retain all 0.1.2 features; add NVIDIA stereo VRS as an
alternative to quad views, with eye tracking and a fixed fallback. Exclude the
unfinished SPS research branch. Preserve the existing opt-in CPU upload
experiments and explain options and performance tradeoffs in hover help.

Base is origin/main c38d6b4. Quad remains the default. VRS keeps two native
stereo views and their submission poses; it creates no quad swapchains and
performs no extra focus scene traversals. The existing bounded world-sort scopes
control NVAPI shading. A per-eye 16-pixel tile map keeps the focus rectangle at
1x1 and shades peripheral tiles at selectable 1x1, 2x2 or 4x4. Overlapping tiles
remain sharp. UI, shadows and unverified passes retain ordinary shading.

Auto gaze uses XR_EXT_eye_gaze_interaction when the runtime supplies it, with
per-frame pose validation and projection into each eye's tangent FOV. Missing,
inactive or invalid tracking selects the configured fixed focus for that frame.
No gaze history is persisted. Existing focus sizes and signed offsets apply.

The launcher isolates known conflicting quad/toolkit layers in the child
process. It preserves saved quad settings but disables quad-only controls in
VRS mode. VRS uses the game's/runtime's ordinary stereo resolution and in-game
crop; mod quad crop remains available in quad mode. Existing benchmark overlay,
input bindings, diagnostics, report generation and motion-corrected submission
remain intact. Unsupported NVAPI hardware or driver failure retains full-rate
stereo and reports the fallback; no improvement is promised.

Alternative considered: VRS on quad outer images retains four traversals and
does not address their CPU cost. Native SPS is unfinished. Stereo VRS is selected
because it can remove the extra traversals without replacing LMU's stereo draws.

Validation: pure map/projection tests, fake gaze lifecycle and XR passthrough
tests, driver-helper tests, launcher settings/environment/layout tests, complete
native/managed builds and hardware smoke test where available. Release notes
must distinguish tests from hardware verification and measured speedups.
